title: Microsoft Teams: two presenters can share screens or windows at the same time in meetings
summary: The rollout window, default and PowerShell commands are supported. The briefing nevertheless treats licensing as wholly unpublished despite documented Teams licensing, and incorrectly casts the general screen-sharing policy's applicability as unconfirmed.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published a licence requirement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace licensing.notes and the first Cost and licensing paragraph with 'Microsoft documents Teams licensing: except for joining meetings anonymously, each user in the organisation needs a Teams license to use Teams. The Teams service description includes meetings and screen sharing across Teams plans. No requirement specific to simultaneous sharing is published at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access and https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/teams-service-description. In the cost rationale and licensing open question, narrow 'licensing is not yet published' to 'a requirement specific to simultaneous sharing is not yet published'.

-AllowMultipleScreenshare
This setting enables Tenant Admins to turn on the Multiple Screenshare feature.
- $false: MultiVBSS meeting options are not available (hidden) for the organizer.
